transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Mina (Redwood Security), Rajiv (CIO, Sable), Lena (Head Security), Owen (Cloud Arch), Priya (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto): deep dive on private vpc security architecture, discuss egress control, k-m-s options, audit logs and soc2 evidence - medium transcript quality

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um today we'll, uh, run through the private/vpc architecture and specifically the security controls around network isolation, ingress and egress, firewalling, and then touch on encryption and compliance. is that the right agenda?
00:12 Rajiv: Yep, that looks good. We've got a couple of folks from infra and security on so happy to dig in.
00:18 Ethan: Quick intro, I'm Ethan, solutions engineer, I'll run the architecture diagrams and mina will cover KMS, key management and audit logs.
00:25 Lena: Great. Quick ask up front, Sable has strict egress rules and we need to understand whether Redwood's control plane will talk out or if everything can be fully private.
00:35 Mina: Yep totally. we'll cover the private control plane options, plus the on-prem package if you need full air gap. note, some of the nomenclature in our docs says "private control plane" vs "managed control plane" which sometimes confuses customers.
00:48 Owen: one quick context item: our network has a default deny posture, transit gateways, and we use a centralized NGFW cluster for egress filtering. we also do VPC peering for some tenants.
01:00 Ethan: Perfect. so the high level: Redwood Private can be deployed in two patterns -- customer-managed VPC with our service nodes deployed in your subnets, or an on-prem appliance bundle for fully air-gapped installs. in the VPC model, the control plane can be configured to be private - either through VPC endpoints or via a private link - and all data plane traffic for inference stays in your network.
01:30 Priya: when you say control plane, does Redwood still need internet outbound for updates/management? we need details for procurement.
01:37 Samira: good question. Options: 1) Fully private control plane using an internal endpoint and a control-plane proxy, 2) Private control plane with restricted egress to a small list of Redwood update endpoints, or 3) fully air-gapped on-prem. we'll send the exact FQDN list for option 2.
01:55 Lena: ok, for Sable we prefer option 1 or 3. option 2 may be ok if we can firewall the FQDNs and maintain strict TLS pinning.
02:05 Mina: For key management, we support Redwood-managed KMS, customer-managed KMS (BYOK) using AWS KMS or Azure KeyVault, and HSM integration for highest assurance. with BYOK you manage the master keys and Redwood only gets wrapped keys.
02:24 Owen: can you expand on the wrapping/rotation model? our security team requires quarterly rotation and audited key use.
02:31 Ethan: Sure. We use envelope encryption. model weights and cache data at rest encrypted with a data key; that data key is wrapped by the CMK in your KMS. rotations happen per your policy; you can trigger rewrap operations. all key use events are recorded in audit logs with KMS request/response traces.
02:52 Lena: are those logs shipped to our SIEM? we want Flow logs plus app-level audit trails.
02:58 Mina: yes. we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 bucket with SSE and then you can pick them up. for VPC level we recommend enabling VPC flow logs to our central collector or to your own account. note, some customers prefer we provide an example lambda to forward logs to their splunk/elk.
03:20 Rajiv: on the firewalling side, how does NAT/egress work for inference nodes? we want to ensure no unintended ops can exfiltrate data to the public internet.
03:30 Ethan: In the customer-managed VPC model, inference nodes are in private subnets with no public IP. egress goes through your NAT or a dedicated egress proxy/NGFW. Redwood's nodes do not require inbound public endpoints. For callbacks (webhooks) we support webhooks via a reverse-proxy pattern or you can configure a web callback via your firewall allow-list.
03:58 Owen: what about model downloads/updates - do they pull from Redwood or from a local mirror? we cannot let model weights be pulled from the internet in production.
04:06 Mina: you can run a local model mirror. Redwood supports model registry mirroring into customer artifact stores (S3/GCS) and then nodes pull from those mirrors over internal network. the default hosted model download will reach out to Redwood if not mirrored, but we recognize regulated customers will mirror.
04:28 Priya: data residency - does any user data leave our region?
04:33 Ethan: No, in the private VPC option, data remains in your VPC and your region. control plane metadata may be routed per your control plane config but for fully private option, metadata focus is kept in-region. we'll share more specifics in the architecture doc.
04:50 Lena: audit timeline: how long are logs retained by default and can we configure retention for compliance?
04:57 Mina: Defaults: 90 days on the Redwood side, but for private deployments we recommend shipping to your archiving bucket and you set retention policy - we don't need to retain logs longer than you require. we can also provide a certified chain of custody export for audit purposes.
05:15 Rajiv: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 - what evidence will you share? vendor attestation or full pack?
05:22 Samira: we share SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, annual pen-test summary, and an evidence bundle for enterprise prospects. for private on-prem customers we can map controls to your audit checklist.
05:35 Lena: ok can you map specifically around multi-tenant isolation and RBAC - how do you ensure tenant A can't access tenant B data?
05:43 Ethan: we enforce logical multi-tenant isolation at multiple layers: network isolation per VPC/subnet, node affinity and containerization boundaries, and per-tenant encryption keys. RBAC is enforced at the platform API layer with role scoping. for private installs you can integrate with your identity provider via SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
06:12 Priya: SSO - do you support SAML and OIDC? group sync?
06:16 Mina: yes SAML 2.0 and OIDC both supported, SCIM for groups and automated provisioning. we map IdP groups to platform roles and you can enable just-in-time access or provisioned accounts. audit trails show who assumed role xyz and timestamps.
06:35 Owen: on network egress restrictions - we use TLS decryption at our NGFW for some traffic - does Redwood support TLS pinning or mTLS for control plane and node communication?
06:44 Ethan: we support mTLS for node-to-control-plane and can support client cert validation. TLS pinning for third-party CAs is trickier but we can give fingerprints for our endpoints and support mutual TLS where required.
07:02 Lena: how granular is RBAC? can we have read-only audit users and separate ops user to trigger model rollouts?
07:08 Mina: Yes. Roles are granular: admin, ops, deployer, auditor, read-only, etc. you can scope roles to projects and models. we'll include example ACL policies in the doc.
07:22 Rajiv: talk to me about ingress - how do you allow customers to send prompts in? through a private API endpoint?
07:29 Ethan: For private VPC we expose internal endpoints (private IPs / internal NLB) that your app can call. you can also front them with your internal API gateway. No public endpoints unless you explicitly enable them.
07:42 Owen: does splitting traffic for dedicated vs burst capacity change the network topology? we plan to use dedicated capacity for latency guarantees but also need occasional bursting to Redwood-hosted pools.
07:52 Samira: we can do hybrid routing. traffic for dedicated capacity stays on private links; for burst we can route to Redwood's dedicated pools over a secure peered connection or via egress filtered endpoints. bursting requires additional egress allowances; we'll diagram this.
08:10 Priya: ok legal will want to see the list of sub processors.
08:13 Samira: yes we'll share the subprocessor list and DPA draft.
08:16 Lena: intrusion detection - do you provide IDS/IPS logs or only node-level metrics?
08:21 Mina: we emit node-level metrics and audit logs. for IDS/IPS you can run your own IDS in-line with flow logs and we can push metadata to your security telemetry. we also support a TAP interface for deeper packet inspection if you choose to set that up.
08:41 Rajiv: specifically on firewall rules, what minimum set do you require for nodes to function in private mode?
08:47 Ethan: minimal egress: access to your KMS endpoints if using BYOK, access to artifact mirror S3 endpoints (if you host mirrors), and if you choose partial control plane, a small set of Redwood update endpoints. we'll provide an allow-list of FQDNs and IPs. inbound: none required except from your internal app subnet.
09:08 Owen: are there recommended healthchecks and synthetic probes to ensure nodes are functioning without opening additional inbound ports?
09:14 Ethan: yes healthcheck via internal NLB health endpoints over internal network and agent heartbeat to the control plane via mTLS outbound. you can also set up private cloudwatch/alarm metrics.
09:28 Lena: do you have data classification hooks - e.g., PII redaction or watermarking?
09:33 Mina: we have content classification hooks and can enable PII scrubbing pre-request or post-response. watermarking is on the roadmap; for now we recommend token-level logging and pattern-based redaction.
09:48 Priya: compliance: can we run a tabletop audit with your security team before procurement sign-off?
09:53 Samira: absolutely. we'll schedule a tabletop and include our security SME.
09:57 (short cross chatter)
10:04 Ethan: ok let's walk through a sample VPC layout - i'll share my screen - sorry audio lag -
10:12 [diagram described] - private subnets for inference nodes, separate mgmt subnet for control-plane proxies, NAT/gateway in a separate egress subnet, S3/GCS mirrors in a storage subnet, and a bastion for admin access to the mgmt subnet.
10:34 Ethan: recommended firewall rules: outbound deny-all, allow egress to KMS:443, artifact-bucket endpoints:443, Redwood updates IPs:443 (if using partial control plane), allow outbound to your SIEM endpoints for log shipping.
11:00 Owen: for bastion access, do you require public IP? we prefer SSM jump or private VPN only.
11:06 Mina: we support SSM Session Manager or private VPN peering into the mgmt subnet; bastion with public IP is optional and not required.
11:15 Rajiv: penetration testing - will Redwood allow us to run an authorized pentest of the deployed nodes?
11:21 Samira: yes under a TBP we can coordinate pentest windows and scoping; for hosted pools it's limited, but for private/on-prem it's standard practice. we'll provide rules of engagement template.
11:33 Lena: about logging - what fields are in the audit events? we need user, action, resource, timestamp, source IP, and correlation IDs.
11:41 Mina: those are included. plus you get KMS key IDs on key operations and request IDs for traceability. correlation IDs propagate through the request lifecycle.
11:55 Priya: SLA related question: how do you handle incident response and notification for private infra?
12:02 Samira: we provide an incident notification SLA in enterprise tiers; for private infra incidents we coordinate via your on-call and runbooks. we also offer optional retained responder blocks.
12:15 Ethan: a couple of gotchas we've seen: 1) forgetting to mirror models and allowing nodes to reach out to public endpoints; 2) misconfigured NAT rules that allow egress to wide CIDR ranges; 3) not enabling flow logs which makes root-cause for alarms harder.
12:35 Owen: noted. can you share a checklist we can pass to our network team?
12:38 Samira: yes checklist + deployment runbook will be shared.
12:42 (brief pause)
12:48 Rajiv: ok let's recap next steps.
12:50 Samira: we will: share architecture diagram and FQDN/IP allow-list; share SOC2/ISO evidence bundle; schedule infra follow-up for NAT/firewall rules; provide example KMS rewrap logs and sample audit exports.
13:05 Lena: we'll send our egress whitelist and compliance questions.
13:08 Priya: legal will review DPA and subprocessor list.
13:12 Samira: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra deep dive.
13:20 (meeting ends)
